title: Joshua 22
paragraphs: ¹ Then Joshua summoned the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh. ² He said to them, "You have carried out everything Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you, and you have obeyed me in all that I commanded you. ³ You have not abandoned your fellow Israelites all this time, right up to this day. You have faithfully kept the charge the LORD your God laid on you. ⁴ Now the LORD your God has given your fellow Israelites rest, as he promised them. So go back home to your own land — the territory that Moses the servant of the LORD gave you east of the Jordan. ⁵ But be very careful to keep the commandment and the law that Moses the servant of the LORD gave you: to love the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways, to keep his commandments, to hold fast to him, and to serve him with all your heart and all your soul."

⁶ Then Joshua blessed them and sent them on their way, and they went home. ⁷ Moses had given the eastern half of the tribe of Manasseh their land in Bashan, while Joshua had given the western half their land among the other tribes west of the Jordan. When Joshua sent them home with his blessing, ⁸ he said, "Go home with great wealth — large herds of livestock, silver, gold, bronze, iron, and a great deal of clothing. Share the plunder from your enemies with your fellow Israelites." ⁹ So the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh left the Israelites at Shiloh in Canaan and headed back to Gilead, their own land, which they had received in accordance with the LORD's command through Moses. ¹⁰ When they reached the region near the Jordan in the land of Canaan, the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh built a large, imposing altar there beside the Jordan.

¹¹ When the rest of the Israelites heard that the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh had built an altar at the edge of Canaan, at the Jordan crossing on the Israelite side, ¹² the whole assembly of Israel gathered at Shiloh, ready to go to war against them. ¹³ But first the Israelites sent Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest to the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead, ¹⁴ accompanied by ten leaders — one senior leader from each of the tribes of Israel, each the head of his family clan. ¹⁵ They came to the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead and said to them,

¹⁶ "This is what the whole assembly of the LORD says: 'What is this act of unfaithfulness you have committed against the God of Israel by turning away from the LORD today and building yourselves an altar in rebellion against him? ¹⁷ Was the sin at Peor not enough for us — a sin from which we have not yet cleansed ourselves, and for which a plague struck the LORD's community? ¹⁸ And now you are turning away from the LORD? If you rebel against the LORD today, tomorrow he will be angry with the whole community of Israel. ¹⁹ If your land is too unclean for you, come over to the LORD's land, where the LORD's tabernacle stands, and take a share among us. But do not rebel against the LORD or against us by building an altar separate from the altar of the LORD our God. ²⁰ When Achan son of Zerah was unfaithful in taking the devoted things, did not God's anger fall on the whole community of Israel? He was not the only one who died for his sin.'"

²¹ The Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh replied to the leaders of the Israelite clans, ²² "The Mighty One, God, the LORD — the Mighty One, God, the LORD — he knows! And let Israel know as well: if this was rebellion or unfaithfulness against the LORD, do not spare us today! ²³ If we built this altar to turn away from the LORD, or to offer burnt offerings or grain offerings on it, or to present fellowship offerings — may the LORD himself call us to account for it. ²⁴ No! We built it out of concern over a future situation. We feared that your descendants might one day say to ours, 'What do you have to do with the LORD, the God of Israel? ²⁵ The LORD set the Jordan as a boundary between us and you Reubenites and Gadites — you have no share in the LORD.' Your descendants might cause ours to stop fearing the LORD.

²⁶ "That is why we said, 'Let us build an altar — not for burnt offerings or sacrifices, ²⁷ but as a witness between us and you and our descendants after us, that we will worship the LORD before him with our burnt offerings, sacrifices, and fellowship offerings. Then in the future your descendants cannot say to ours, "You have no share in the LORD."' ²⁸ We thought, 'If they ever say this to us or to our descendants in the future, we will answer: Look at this replica of the LORD's altar, which our ancestors built — not for burnt offerings and sacrifices, but as a witness between us and you.' ²⁹ Far be it from us to rebel against the LORD and turn away from him today by building an altar for burnt offerings, grain offerings, and sacrifices, separate from the altar of the LORD our God that stands before his tabernacle!" ³⁰ When Phinehas the priest and the leaders of the assembly — the heads of the Israelite clans — heard what the Reubenites, Gadites, and Manassites had to say, they were satisfied.

³¹ Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest said to the Reubenites, Gadites, and Manassites, "Today we know that the LORD is with us, because you have not acted unfaithfully toward the LORD in this matter. You have saved the Israelites from the LORD's judgment." ³² Then Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the leaders returned from the Reubenites and Gadites in Gilead to the land of Canaan and reported back to the Israelites. ³³ The Israelites were pleased with the report and praised God. They said no more about going to war against them, about destroying the land where the Reubenites and Gadites lived. ³⁴ The Reubenites and Gadites named the altar "Witness," saying, "It is a witness between us that the LORD is God."
